source.title: Positive and free boundary solutions to singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption: an overview and open problems

accepted.question_text: For the boundary value problem -Δu + 1/u^α = λ f(x) in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω, where α > 0 (mainly α < 1) and f ≥ 0, does there exist, in addition to the known maximal positive solution for sufficiently large λ, any further solution that is either another positive solution or a compact-support (free-boundary) solution?

evidence.quote: -Δu + 1/u^α = λ f(x) in Ω, u = 0 on ∂Ω, where 0 < α (mainly α < 1) and f ≥ 0.
but it remains the problem of the possible existence of more solutions, either positive or with compact support.

accepted.question_text: In the radial-domain case Ω = B_r(0) for problem (II), namely -Δu + 1/u^α = λ u^p in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω, α > 0 (mainly α < 1), and 0 < p < 1, are there non-radial solutions even though the cited analysis only treats radial ones?

evidence.quote: Also we will consider problem (II): -Δu + 1/u^α = λ u^p in Ω, u = 0 on ∂Ω, with 0 < α (mainly α < 1) and 0 < p < 1.
since the famous Gidas-Ni-Nirenberg theorem is not applicable, existence of non-radial solutions cannot be excluded.

accepted.question_text: For the radial solutions of problem (II) on Ω = B_r(0), where the cited work finds two radial solutions for λ* < λ < λ** and only the upper branch for λ > λ**, what mechanism explains why the lower radial branch stops at λ = λ** when the branch otherwise stays inside the positive cone and reaches zero normal derivative there?

evidence.quote: there are two radial solutions u1 and u2 verifying u1 < u2 and for λ > λ** there is only the solution u2.
Here we have a complete description of radial solutions, and we may ask why the branch "stops" at the value λ = λ**.

accepted.question_text: In the one-dimensional quasilinear problem -( |u'|^{p-2}u')' = f(u) on Ω = (-1,1) with u(±1)=0, under the integrability assumption (B) and in the model case f(u)=λu^β-u^α with -1 < α < β < p-1, is there a unique threshold α* such that there is exactly one solution for α in (-1, α*] and exactly two solutions for α in (α*, -1/p + 1)?

evidence.quote: We consider now the one-dimensional quasilinear boundary value problem -( |u'| ^{p-2}u')' = f(u) in Ω = (-1,1), u(±1)=0.
It is reasonable to guess that there should be a unique α* such that there is only one solution on (-1, α*] and two on (α*,-1/p+1). We were unable to prove that this happens in general.

accepted.question_text: For the problem -Δu + u^α = λu^β in a star-shaped domain Ω, with u = 0 on ∂Ω, 0 < α < β < 1, and N > 2(1+α)(1+β)/((1-α)(1-β)), the cited result gives, for some λ, a positive solution w_λ with ∂w_λ/∂n ≠ 0 on ∂Ω. Must that solution in fact satisfy the stronger boundary inequality ∂w_λ/∂n ≤ 0 on ∂Ω?

evidence.quote: -Δu + u^α = λu^β in Ω, u = 0 on ∂Ω, with 0 < α < β < 1. Now Ω is a star-shaped domain and the condition N > 2(1+α)(1+β)/(1-α)(1-β) is also satisfied.
One could think that in the first case we actually have ∂w_λ/∂n ≤ 0 on ∂Ω.

accepted.question_text: In the same star-shaped-domain problem -Δu + u^α = λu^β with 0 < α < β < 1 and N > 2(1+α)(1+β)/((1-α)(1-β)), the cited result also gives, for some λ, a nonnegative solution u_λ with zero normal derivative on the boundary. Is that solution actually strictly positive in Ω?

evidence.quote: (ii) there exists a solution u_λ ≥ 0 such that ∂u_λ/∂n = 0 on ∂Ω.
One could think that in the first case we actually have ∂w_λ/∂n ≤ 0 on ∂Ω and in the second u_λ > 0.

accepted.question_text: For the approximating problem -Δu + u^q/(u+ε)^(q+α) = λu^p in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω, where ε > 0 and 0 < q < p, if the minimizers u_ε converge as ε → 0 to a nonnegative solution u, is the limit solution u necessarily strictly positive in Ω?
accepted.context_brief: Approximation scheme positivity of limit minimizer

evidence.quote: -Δu + u^q/(u+ε)^(q+α) = λu^p in Ω, u = 0 on ∂Ω.
One can guess that u > 0 and that maybe v has compact support, but this is not proved in the paper.

accepted.question_text: For the same approximating problem -Δu + u^q/(u+ε)^(q+α) = λu^p in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω, where ε > 0 and 0 < q < p, the cited work produces a second critical point v_ε converging as ε → 0 to a nonnegative solution v. Does the limit solution v have compact support?
accepted.context_brief: Approximation scheme compact support of second branch

evidence.quote: Then he proves that this functional has a minimum u_ε ≥ 0 and also a second critical point v_ε ≥ 0 ... and that when ε goes to 0 they tend to ... solutions u ≥ 0 and v ≥ 0.
One can guess that u > 0 and that maybe v has compact support, but this is not proved in the paper.

accepted.question_text: Consider problem (III), -Δu = K(x)(λu^β - u^α) in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω, where K(x)=1/d(x)^k, 0 < k < 2, and 0 < α < β < 1, together with its p-Laplacian generalization discussed later in the paper. In the regime k-α < 1, is there more than one positive solution?

evidence.quote: -Δu = K(x)(λu^β-u^α) in Ω, u = 0 on ∂Ω, with K(x)=1/d(x)^k with 0<k<2 and 0<α<β<1.
it would be interesting to know if there is more than one positive solution in the first case k-α<1

accepted.question_text: For problem (III), -Δu = K(x)(λu^β - u^α) in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω, K(x)=1/d(x)^k, 0 < k < 2, and 0 < α < β < 1, and likewise for the p-Laplacian generalization mentioned in the paper, do compact-support solutions exist in the regime k-α < 1?

evidence.quote: (i) If k-α<1, there exists λ* such that for all λ>λ* there is a solution u_λ>0 to (III) and there is no solution for λ small; (ii) If 1<k-α<2 there exists at least a solution with compact support for all λ>λ**.
and if, also in this case, there are compact support solutions.

accepted.question_text: For the compact-support solutions associated with problem (III), namely -Δu = K(x)(λu^β - u^α) in Ω with K(x)=1/d(x)^k, 0 < k < 2, and 0 < α < β < 1, what is the structure of the set of compact-support solutions?

evidence.quote: Now we study the problem -Δu = K(x)(λu^β-u^α) in Ω, u=0 on ∂Ω, with K(x)=1/d(x)^k with 0<k<2 and 0<α<β<1.
Information on the structure of the set of compact support solutions is interesting as well.

accepted.question_text: For the singular nonlinear elliptic and free-boundary problems discussed in this survey, what multiplicity results remain valid when the diffusion term is replaced by other operators, including a general linear second-order elliptic operator, the p-Laplacian, Hamilton-Jacobi type operators, the Monge-Ampère operator, the bi-Laplacian, or operators arising in nonlinear systems or Schrödinger systems?

evidence.quote: Finally, in Section 5 we present a short list of some interesting open problems in the theory. Again, they concern principally the possible multiplicity of positive solutions and of free boundary solutions in general domains in R^N for N>1.

Multiplicity for different diffusion operators (not only a general linear second order operator or the p-Laplacian operator, but other nonlinear operators of Hamilton-Jacobi type, Monge-Ampère, bi-Laplacian, nonlinear systems, Schroedinger systems, etc.)

accepted.question_text: For the elliptic problems of the kind surveyed in this paper, how do the existence, multiplicity, and free-boundary phenomena change when measures appear in the equation not only as source data but also as coefficients of zero-order terms or in similarly singular roles?

evidence.quote: We give a survey of recent results and open problems concerning existence and multiplicity of positive and/or compact support solutions to some semilinear elliptic equations with singular nonlinear terms of absorption type.
Presence of measures at the equation (not only as a sourcing data but also as coefficients of zero order terms, . . . )

trace.notes: Resolved zbMATH record 6283635 to the EJDE open-access article and mapped the PDF. The explicit open-problem list is in Section 5 on article pages 41-42, with additional unresolved questions on pages 35, 36, and 40.
Extracted two unresolved questions from Section 2: additional solutions for problem (I), and non-radial/branch-stopping questions for the radial study of problem (II).
Extracted the unproved unique-threshold α* conjecture from the unified one-dimensional case in Section 4.

Extracted all explicit open problems listed in Section 5, including the star-shaped-domain refinements, approximation-limit questions, problem (III) multiplicity/compact-support questions, operator-generalization multiplicity, and measure-valued extensions.
Rewrote each candidate into a self-contained question by inlining the governing PDE, parameter regime, and the specific unknown asserted by the source text.
Kept closely related but distinct questions separate when they asked about different properties, for example positivity versus compact support, or multiplicity versus structure of the solution set.

All accepted items have explicit source evidence with article page numbers and were checked to remove dangling references to problem numbers or case labels by expanding those references into standalone formulations.
